**Gram-positive cocci (Staphylococcus aureus):** IV vancomycin + joint drainage
**Crystals present with negative Gram stain:** crystal-induced arthropathy
Serial joint drainage via needle aspiration or arthroscopy
Tailor intravenous antibiotic regimen to synovial culture results

**Advanced stage (Rai III-IV) or bulky disease:** targeted therapy (ibrutinib or venetoclax)
Infection prophylaxis: pneumococcal and influenza vaccines, avoid live vaccines

UWSA1:Q005.boardCall: Parenteral nutrition via central line -> Bloodstream infection
UWSA1:Q005.hinge: Central venous catheterization for parenteral nutrition carries central line-associated bloodstream infection as its most frequent and serious complication.
UWSA1:Q005.trap: Nutritional therapy initiation tempts refeeding syndrome, but that occurs in severely malnourished patients, whereas this patient had a normal BMI.

A.clue: Central venous catheter-related bacteremia or fungemia
A.fit: Here: parenteral nutrition started through a central venous catheter

B.clue: Gallbladder sludge and stone formation from biliary stasis
B.fit: Not here: develops after weeks of parenteral nutrition, not acutely

C.clue: Hypervolemia from excessive parenteral infusion volume
C.fit: Not here: normal cardiac and renal function, BMI 26 kg/m2

D.clue: Low blood glucose from abrupt parenteral nutrition cessation
D.fit: Not here: occurs upon abrupt cessation, hyperglycemia is more common

E.clue: Severe hypophosphatemia upon feeding chronically starved patient
E.fit: Not here: previously healthy man with normal baseline BMI 26 kg/m2

nodes.text: Parenteral nutrition through a central catheter increases bloodstream infection risk.
Prevent infection with sterile insertion, chlorhexidine preparation, hub care, and daily line-necessity review.
Monitor glucose, electrolytes, liver tests, and catheter site; transition to enteral nutrition when feasible.
**Fever or catheter inflammation:** obtain paired peripheral/line cultures; start vancomycin plus cefepime for suspected sepsis.
**Candida, S aureus, Pseudomonas, shock, or persistent bacteremia:** remove the line and give organism-directed IV therapy.
**Stable selected coagulase-negative staphylococcal long-term line infection:** consider systemic antibiotics plus antibiotic lock.

algorithm.title: Acute psychotic agitation in emergency department

nodes.text: Acute psychotic agitation threatening staff: attempt verbal de-escalation
**Imminent violence despite de-escalation:** physical restraint + IM antipsychotic
IM haloperidol, ziprasidone, or olanzapine
**Still agitated 30 min after IM antipsychotic:** add IM lorazepam (not with IM olanzapine)
**Stimulant intoxication or alcohol withdrawal:** IM lorazepam preferred
Continuous monitoring: vitals, pulse oximetry, airway, restraint checks; remove restraints promptly
Once calm: glucose, toxicology, electrolytes; head CT if trauma or focal deficits

algorithm.title: Painless lower gastrointestinal bleeding in toddler

nodes.text: Painless large maroon stool in toddler: suspect Meckel diverticulum
Ectopic gastric mucosa secretes acid, ulcerating adjacent ileum
Technetium-99m pertechnetate scan detects ectopic gastric mucosa

**Scan negative, suspicion persists:** repeat scan with H2 blocker or diagnostic laparoscopy
**Colicky pain with currant-jelly stool:** ultrasound for intussusception with Meckel lead point
Diverticulectomy or segmental ileal resection including ulcerated bowel

B.tempting: metabolic acidosis can stem from renal loss

C.fit: Not here: vomiting causes metabolic alkalosis, not acidemia pH 7.24
C.tempting: patient had an episode of vomiting

D.clue: Accelerated ketogenesis causing diabetic ketoacidosis
D.fit: Not here: fingerstick blood glucose is only 154 mg/dL

nodes.text: Septic shock: fever, BP 70/60 mm Hg, warm extremities, pneumonia source
Hypoperfusion → anaerobic glycolysis: increased tissue metabolic (lactic) acid production
Blood cultures + lactate, then broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour
IV crystalloid bolus
**MAP < 65 mm Hg after fluid bolus:** norepinephrine
**MAP < 65 mm Hg despite norepinephrine:** add vasopressin + hydrocortisone
**Initial lactate ≥ 2 mmol/L:** repeat lactate within 2–6 h to guide resuscitation
Chest x-ray to confirm aspiration pneumonia source

nodes.text: Recognize DIC: acute thrombocytopenia, elevated INR, low fibrinogen, elevated LDH, reticulocytosis
Peripheral blood smear: schistocytes confirming microangiopathic hemolytic anemia
Treat underlying malignancy or precipitating systemic infection
**Active bleeding or high procedure risk with platelets < 50,000/mm3:** transfuse platelets
**Hypofibrinogenemia (< 150 mg/dL) with active hemorrhage:** infuse cryoprecipitate
**Prolonged INR with active hemorrhage:** administer fresh frozen plasma
Avoid antifibrinolytic agents (tranexamic acid) due to risk of fatal thrombosis

nodes.text: Confirm anovulatory infertility in PCOS: oligomenorrhea, hyperandrogenism, and metabolic obesity
Prescribe structured lifestyle modification and weight loss as the first-line intervention
**Persistent anovulation despite weight reduction:** initiate ovulation induction with oral letrozole (aromatase inhibitor)
**Second-line ovulation induction:** administer clomiphene citrate or exogenous gonadotropin injections
**Patients not desiring immediate pregnancy:** prescribe combined oral contraceptive pills for cycle regulation and hirsutism
Screen all PCOS patients for metabolic comorbidities: 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test and lipid profile

**Sensory deficit over dorsal cutaneous and hypothenar regions:** localizes compression to the elbow (cubital tunnel)
**Sensory deficit restricted to palmar digits with intact dorsal sensation:** localizes compression to the wrist (Guyon canal)

**Progressive motor weakness or persistent sensory loss despite splinting:** surgical decompression or anterior transposition

nodes.text: Severe hypertriglyceridemia causes recurrent pancreatitis; long-term triglyceride lowering prevents recurrence.
Start fenofibrate to lower triglycerides below 500 mg/dL.
Avoid alcohol, reduce dietary fat, and address diabetes and secondary causes.
**Acute pancreatitis:** IV fluids, analgesia, and early enteral feeding as tolerated.
**Uncontrolled hyperglycemia:** insulin also accelerates triglyceride clearance.
**Triglycerides remain ≥500 despite fenofibrate and lifestyle changes:** add prescription omega-3 fatty acids.
**Elevated LDL or high ASCVD risk:** add statin; prefer fenofibrate over gemfibrozil with statins.

UWSA1:Q123.boardCall: Irregular heartbeat + progressive PR prolongation followed by dropped QRS -> Mobitz type I second-degree AV block (Wenckebach).
UWSA1:Q123.hinge: Progressive lengthening of PR intervals until a single P wave fails to conduct to the ventricles defines Mobitz I second-degree AV block.
UWSA1:Q123.trap: First-degree AV block has prolonged PR intervals that are constant with no dropped beats; Mobitz II has fixed PR with dropped beats.

A.fit: Not here: distinct, uniform P waves precede conducted QRS complexes on rhythm strip

B.fit: Not here: nonconducted P wave occurs after progressive lengthening of PR interval

C.clue: Abnormal early P wave with incomplete pause
C.fit: Not here: sinus P waves occur at regular intervals with progressive PR prolongation

D.clue: Progressive PR lengthening preceding dropped QRS complex
D.fit: Here: regular sinus P waves with increasing PR intervals until a dropped QRS

E.clue: Short PR interval with delta wave
E.fit: Not here: absence of short PR interval (< 120 ms) or initial delta wave slurring

nodes.text: Analyze 12-lead ECG: relationship between P waves, PR interval duration, and QRS conduction
**First-degree AV block (fixed PR > 200 ms, no dropped QRS):** benign, observation only
**Mobitz type I second-degree AV block (progressive PR prolongation, dropped QRS):** observation in asymptomatic patients; review AV nodal drugs
**Mobitz type II second-degree AV block (constant PR, unpredictable dropped QRS):** high risk of complete block; place permanent pacemaker
**Third-degree complete AV block (complete AV dissociation):** emergent temporary transvenous pacing followed by permanent pacemaker
Review medications: discontinue or reduce AV-nodal blocking agents (beta blockers, verapamil, diltiazem, digoxin)

algorithm.title: Peripheral artery disease and ischemic ulceration

nodes.text: Suspect PAD with distal nonhealing ulcers, trophic changes, or exertional limb pain.
Measure resting ankle-brachial index using Doppler ultrasound.
**ABI ≤0.90:** confirm PAD; assess symptoms and tissue loss separately from ABI severity.
**ABI >1.40:** obtain toe-brachial index for noncompressible arteries.
Start high-intensity statin, aspirin or clopidogrel, blood pressure control, and smoking cessation.
**Stable claudication without tissue loss:** prescribe structured walking exercise.
**Ischemic rest pain or nonhealing ulcer/gangrene:** arrange prompt vascular evaluation for revascularization.

nodes.text: Identify characteristic physical exam: midsystolic flow murmur at left upper sternal border with wide, fixed split S2
Interatrial communication drives left-to-right intracardiac shunting, overloading right atrium and ventricle
Obtain transthoracic echocardiogram with bubble study to confirm interatrial defect and quantify shunt ratio (Qp:Qs)
**Significant left-to-right shunt (Qp:Qs ≥ 1.5:1 or RV enlargement):** perform transcatheter or surgical closure
Monitor for long-term complications: atrial arrhythmias (flutter, fibrillation) and paradoxical thromboembolic strokes
**Untreated severe pulmonary arterial hypertension with shunt reversal (Eisenmenger syndrome):** closure is contraindicated; start pulmonary vasodilators

nodes.text: Suspect primary hyperaldosteronism: treatment-resistant hypertension or unprovoked/thiazide-induced profound hypokalemia
Screening: calculate morning plasma aldosterone concentration to plasma renin activity ratio (PAC/PRA > 20)
Confirm autonomous secretion: oral salt loading or saline suppression test demonstrating failure of aldosterone suppression
Perform adrenal CT imaging to differentiate unilateral adrenal adenoma from bilateral adrenal cortical hyperplasia
**Bilateral adrenal hyperplasia or non-surgical candidate:** initiate medical therapy with spironolactone or eplerenone
**Unilateral aldosterone-producing adenoma:** perform adrenal venous sampling followed by laparoscopic unilateral adrenalectomy

UWSA1:Q136.trap: Late or cold septic shock can show low cardiac output, but acute warm septic shock demonstrates high cardiac index and low SVR.

A.clue: Cardiogenic shock with elevated PCWP and low CI
A.fit: Not here: warm extremity with bounding pulses indicates hyperdynamic distributive shock rather than cardiogenic pump failure

B.clue: Hypovolemic shock with low preload and high SVR
B.fit: Not here: warm extremities and bounding pulses indicate distributive shock

C.clue: Low PCWP, low cardiac index, and elevated SVR
C.fit: Not here: systemic vascular resistance is markedly reduced in septic distributive shock due to inflammatory vasodilation

D.clue: Distributive septic shock with hyperdynamic cardiac output
D.fit: Here: cellulitis, BP 80/52, bounding pulses, warm extremities, elevated lactate, leukocytosis 18,000

E.clue: High preload, high output, low SVR
E.fit: Not here: venodilation and capillary leak in sepsis decrease central venous and pulmonary capillary wedge pressures

F.clue: Elevated biventricular filling with depressed SVR and SvO2
F.fit: Not here: warm extremities reflect hyperdynamic state with increased mixed venous oxygen

nodes.text: Hypotension with warm extremities and bounding pulses: distributive (septic) shock
Low SVR, high cardiac output, low-normal PCWP, high mixed venous O2 saturation

**Low output, low PCWP, high SVR:** hypovolemic shock; fluids or blood
Cultures, broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour, crystalloid bolus
**MAP < 65 mm Hg despite fluids:** norepinephrine infusion

UWSA1:Q137.hinge: Upper respiratory tract involvement (hearing loss, otitis), glomerulonephritis, and cutaneous ulceration (pyoderma gangrenosum-like or leukocytoclastic vasculitis) indicate systemic necrotizing vasculitis.

B.fit: Not here: lack of chronic hemolytic anemia and presence of active glomerulonephritis and otitis

**Dialysis dependence, rapidly rising creatinine, or anti-GBM overlap:** consider adjunctive plasma exchange
**Remission achieved:** use rituximab or azathioprine maintenance; methotrexate requires adequate renal function

algorithm.title: Cholelithiasis after rapid weight loss (Bariatric surgery)

nodes.text: Evaluate postprandial right upper quadrant pain radiating to shoulder following bariatric surgery
Recognize rapid massive weight loss as the primary risk factor promoting biliary cholesterol supersaturation and gallstone formation
Prophylaxis: treat with oral ursodeoxycholic acid (ursodiol) for 6 months postoperatively following bariatric surgery
Diagnostic imaging: perform right upper quadrant ultrasound to evaluate for gallstones, acoustic shadowing, and gallbladder wall thickening
**Symptomatic cholelithiasis or acute cholecystitis:** perform laparoscopic cholecystectomy
**Suspected choledocholithiasis:** note that altered anatomy precludes standard ERCP; use transgastric or surgical exploration

UWSA1:Q141.hinge: Identification of glomerular bleeding (RBC casts, dysmorphic RBCs) requires quantifying proteinuria to evaluate for glomerulonephritis or nephrotic-range disease.
UWSA1:Q141.trap: Nonglomerular hematuria (stones, cancer) requires CT urography and cystoscopy; glomerular hematuria does not require urological CT.

UWSA1:Q143.boardCall: End-stage renal disease + hypocalcemia + hyperphosphatemia + bone pain (renal osteodystrophy) -> Secondary hyperparathyroidism -> Parathyroid glandular hyperplasia.
UWSA1:Q143.hinge: Chronic phosphate retention and impaired 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D synthesis lead to hypocalcemia, causing compensatory hyperplasia of all four parathyroid glands.
UWSA1:Q143.trap: Single parathyroid adenoma causes primary hyperparathyroidism with hypercalcemia; ESRD causes secondary hyperplasia of all glands with low/normal calcium.

A.clue: Autoimmune destruction of parathyroid glands causing hypocalcemia
A.fit: Not here: ESRD induces compensatory parathyroid hormone hypersecretion, not autoimmune gland destruction

B.clue: Noncaseating granulomatous invasion of parathyroid tissue
B.fit: Not here: sarcoidosis causes hypercalcemia via extrarenal calcitriol synthesis, not hypocalcemia with bone pain

C.clue: Glandular involution secondary to autonomous hypercalcemia
C.fit: Not here: hypocalcemia (7.9 mg/dL) stimulates parathyroid proliferation, leading to glandular hyperplasia

D.clue: Four-gland cellular hyperplasia driven by hypocalcemia
D.fit: Here: ESRD on hemodialysis, bone pain, low calcium 7.9 mg/dL, high phosphorus 6.1 mg/dL

E.clue: Autonomous solitary adenoma causing primary hyperparathyroidism
E.fit: Not here: single adenoma causes hypercalcemia; ESRD induces diffuse four-gland hyperplasia with low calcium

algorithm.title: Secondary hyperparathyroidism in chronic kidney disease

nodes.text: CKD causes phosphate retention and reduced calcitriol, producing hypocalcemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism.
Chronic stimulation causes diffuse hyperplasia of all four parathyroid glands.
**Persistently elevated phosphate:** restrict dietary phosphate and give phosphate binders.
**Severe progressive PTH elevation despite corrected phosphate and vitamin D:** consider calcitriol.
**Receiving dialysis:** consider calcimimetics or active vitamin D; target PTH approximately 2–9 times normal.
**Autonomous hyperparathyroidism with hypercalcemia despite medical treatment:** parathyroidectomy.

nodes.text: Identify acute delirium: fluctuating cognitive impairment, inattention, and perceptual disturbances triggered by medical illness
First-line nonpharmacological de-escalation: frequent reorientation, family presence, sitter, quiet room, and minimize tethers
Administer low-dose haloperidol for severe acute agitation threatening self or staff safety (physical violence, pulling lines)
**Alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal delirium:** administer intravenous lorazepam or diazepam instead of antipsychotics
**Urinary tract infection present:** initiate empiric antibacterial therapy
Review and discontinue deliriogenic medications: anticholinergics, sedatives, opioids, and antihistamines

nodes.text: Suspect myelodysplastic syndrome in an older patient with unexplained cytopenias and macrocytic anemia
Review peripheral blood smear demonstrating dysplastic changes (ovalomacrocytes, hyposegmented/hypogranulated neutrophils)
Perform bone marrow aspiration and biopsy with cytogenetics to confirm hypercellular marrow, dysplasia, and blast count
**Risk stratification:** use revised International Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS-R) based on cytogenetics, blasts, and cytopenias
**Lower-risk MDS:** supportive transfusions + erythropoiesis-stimulating agents or luspatercept for transfusion dependence
**Higher-risk MDS or excess blasts:** treat with hypomethylating agents (azacitidine, decitabine) or allogeneic stem cell transplantation

**Contraindicated medications:** avoid anticholinergic/muscarinic antagonists and tricyclics, which paralyze detrusor contractility
Screen for secondary complications: monitor for recurrent urinary tract infections, hydronephrosis, and progressive renal insufficiency

UWSA1:Q148.trap: Vegetations cause acute infective endocarditis with regurgitant murmurs and systemic fever; dystrophic calcification is the mechanism of chronic senile stenosis.

Age > 70: dystrophic calcification of trileaflet aortic valve causes stenosis
TTE: jet velocity, mean gradient, valve area, EF
**Velocity ≥ 4 m/s with angina, syncope, or dyspnea:** SAVR or TAVR
**Velocity ≥ 4 m/s, asymptomatic, EF < 50%:** aortic valve replacement
**Velocity < 4 m/s, asymptomatic:** serial echocardiography every 1–2 years
**Fever + new murmur:** blood cultures for endocarditis
Statins do not slow calcific AS progression

algorithm.title: Comparing multiple group means with ANOVA

**Confidence interval includes 0 (null value):** pairwise difference is not statistically significant

algorithm.title: Calculating odds ratios in case-control studies

nodes.text: Construct 2x2 contingency table: disease status (columns) vs exposure status (rows)
Assign cell counts: a = exposed cases, b = exposed controls, c = unexposed cases, d = unexposed controls
Compute odds ratio using cross-product: OR = (a * d) / (b * c)
**OR = 1.0:** exposure is not associated with altered odds of disease
**OR > 1.0:** exposure is associated with increased odds of disease
**OR < 1.0:** exposure is associated with decreased odds of disease
Interpret 95% confidence interval: statistically significant if interval excludes 1.0

algorithm.title: Understanding statistical power and type II error

nodes.text: Define statistical power (1 - beta): probability of detecting a true effect when one exists
Identify determinants of power: sample size, significance level (alpha), and anticipated effect size
**Large effect size (e.g., >=10%):** requires smaller sample size to achieve 80% power
**Small effect size (e.g., <10%):** requires much larger sample size to avoid type II error
Evaluate nonsignificant study result (p >= 0.05) with zero attrition
**True difference smaller than expected:** study lacked power to detect subtle effect (type II error)
**No true difference exists:** null hypothesis is genuinely correct

Vascular surgery + two large-bore IVs + blood products; permissive hypotension
**Known AAA + SBP < 90 mm Hg:** straight to operating room without imaging
**SBP < 90 mm Hg, AAA not known:** bedside ultrasound for aorta > 3 cm
**SBP ≥ 90 mm Hg:** CT angiography to confirm rupture and plan EVAR
Repair: EVAR if anatomy suitable, otherwise open repair

UWSA1:Q030.boardCall: Knee osteoarthritis + acute effusion and warmth despite NSAIDs -> Arthrocentesis
UWSA1:Q030.hinge: When chronic osteoarthritis develops a new effusion with warmth, arthrocentesis must be performed to exclude crystal arthropathy or septic arthritis before injecting steroids.
UWSA1:Q030.trap: Refractory osteoarthritis tempts immediate intraarticular corticosteroid injection, but injecting steroids into a warm joint before ruling out infection via arthrocentesis is hazardous.

A.clue: Synovial fluid aspiration for cell count, crystals, culture
A.fit: Here: worsened knee pain, new effusion and warmth despite naproxen

B.clue: High-potency NSAID with gastrointestinal toxicity risk
B.fit: Not here: failed naproxen, presence of effusion requires diagnostic aspiration

C.clue: Local anti-inflammatory injection for refractory non-infected OA
C.fit: Not here: must exclude septic arthritis and crystals before injecting steroids
C.tempting: standard next step for refractory osteoarthritis

D.clue: Total knee arthroplasty for end-stage joint destruction
D.fit: Not here: conservative medical options and diagnostic aspiration not yet exhausted
D.tempting: severe pain limiting activities of daily living

E.clue: Microtubule inhibitor for acute crystal-induced flare
E.fit: Not here: crystal arthropathy not yet confirmed by synovial fluid analysis
E.tempting: warmth and effusion resemble acute gout

nodes.text: Osteoarthritis with acute worsening: examine for joint effusion, warmth, and erythema
Perform diagnostic and therapeutic arthrocentesis before intraarticular injection
Synovial fluid analysis: leukocyte count with differential, Gram stain, culture, crystals
**WBC < 2,000/mm3 without crystals:** intraarticular corticosteroid injection
**Positively birefringent rhomboid crystals (pseudogout):** intraarticular steroid or oral colchicine
**WBC > 50,000/mm3 or positive Gram stain (septic arthritis):** intravenous antibiotics + joint drainage
Consider total joint arthroplasty if refractory end-stage osteoarthritis severely impairs daily living

UWSA1:Q031.boardCall: Weight loss + stable appetite + new atrial fibrillation HR 142 -> TSH and free T4
UWSA1:Q031.hinge: Unexplained weight loss accompanied by new-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response is a classic presentation of hyperthyroidism.
UWSA1:Q031.trap: Severe hypertension and tachycardia tempt urine metanephrines for pheochromocytoma, but hyperthyroidism is significantly more common.

A.clue: Measures hypercortisolemia in suspected Cushing syndrome
A.fit: Not here: unintentional weight loss and tachycardia, not central obesity

B.clue: Vagal stimulation test assessing carotid baroreceptors
B.fit: Not here: persistent tachyarrhythmia pulse 142/min and weight loss
B.tempting: episodes of dizziness in elderly male

C.clue: Graded exercise ECG assessing coronary ischemia
C.fit: Not here: resting atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate 142/min
C.tempting: dizziness and hypertension in former smoker

D.clue: Screening test for primary hyperaldosteronism
D.fit: Not here: hyperthyroid features with weight loss and rapid atrial fibrillation

E.clue: Orthostatic challenge assessing autonomic syncope
E.fit: Not here: resting tachyarrhythmia with pulse 142/min and weight loss

F.clue: Initial serum screening for hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis
F.fit: Here: new atrial fibrillation HR 142/min, weight loss, hypertension

G.clue: Screening test for catecholamine-secreting pheochromocytoma
G.fit: Not here: thyroid dysfunction is far more common cause of atrial fibrillation
G.tempting: hypertension and tachycardia with weight loss

algorithm.title: New-onset atrial fibrillation with systemic symptoms

nodes.text: New atrial fibrillation with rapid rate + weight loss: screen for hyperthyroidism
Check TSH + free T4, basic metabolic panel
**Hypotension, chest pain, or pulmonary edema:** synchronized cardioversion
**Low TSH with elevated free T4:** propranolol + methimazole
Rate control with beta-blocker or diltiazem
ECG and transthoracic echocardiogram for structural heart disease
CHA2DS2-VASc score to decide anticoagulation

UWSA1:Q032.boardCall: Exertional dyspnea + bibasilar crackles + FEV1/FVC 85% + FVC 58% -> Lung stiffening due to fibrosis
UWSA1:Q032.hinge: Bibasilar fine crackles and a restrictive spirometric defect (reduced FVC with preserved FEV1/FVC > 70%) indicate interstitial pulmonary fibrosis.
UWSA1:Q032.trap: A 30-pack-year smoking history tempts COPD/emphysema, but the spirometry is restrictive (FEV1/FVC 85%) rather than obstructive.

A.clue: Inadequate minute ventilation causing hypercapnic respiratory failure
A.fit: Not here: bibasilar fine crackles and normal FEV1/FVC ratio 85%

B.clue: Goblet cell hyperplasia with chronic productive cough
B.fit: Not here: nonproductive cough and restrictive spirometry with FEV1/FVC 85%

C.clue: Protease-mediated destruction of interalveolar septa
C.fit: Not here: obstructive pattern with low FEV1/FVC is absent

D.clue: Smooth muscle hypertrophy and eosinophilic airway inflammation
D.fit: Not here: fine bibasilar crackles and irreversible restrictive spirometry

E.clue: Elevated left ventricular filling pressures causing pulmonary edema
E.fit: Not here: normal JVP, normal ECG, and restrictive pulmonary defect

F.clue: Excessive collagen deposition decreasing lung compliance
F.fit: Here: bibasilar fine crackles, FEV1/FVC 85%, FVC 58% of predicted

nodes.text: Recognize interstitial lung disease: progressive exertional dyspnea, dry cough, bibasilar fine crackles
Alveolar epithelial injury and fibroblast activation drive lung stiffening due to fibrosis
Pulmonary function testing: restrictive pattern (FEV1/FVC > 70%, reduced TLC and FVC)
High-resolution chest CT (HRCT): subpleural reticulation, traction bronchiectasis, and honeycombing
**Definite UIP pattern on HRCT:** diagnose idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis without surgical lung biopsy
Initiate antifibrotic therapy (pirfenidone or nintedanib) to slow disease progression
Smoking cessation + supplemental oxygen for resting or exertional hypoxemia (SpO2 ≤ 88%)

UWSA1:Q033.hinge: Pseudoclaudication posture-dependent pain with intact pulses indicates spinal stenosis, diagnosed by lumbar MRI.
UWSA1:Q033.trap: Decreased ankle vibration tempts nerve conduction studies for diabetic neuropathy, but the classic posture-dependent pseudoclaudication is lumbar stenosis.

A.tempting: exertional leg pain in patient with vascular risk factors

B.fit: Not here: postural leg pain worse walking downhill, normal muscle strength
B.tempting: elderly male with back and leg pain

C.fit: Here: leg pain worse walking downhill, relieved sitting, normal pulses

D.clue: Evaluates nerve action potential velocity and amplitude
D.fit: Not here: neurogenic claudication with postural relief, MRI confirms canal stenosis
D.tempting: absent ankle reflexes and decreased vibration sensation

E.fit: Not here: pain radiates down posterior thigh and improves with spinal flexion
E.tempting: exertional leg pain in older adult

nodes.text: Bilateral leg pain worse with extension, relieved by flexion: neurogenic claudication
Normal pulses distinguish from vascular claudication; ABI not needed
MRI of lumbosacral spine establishes canal narrowing
Flexion-based physical therapy + NSAIDs
**Radicular pain despite 6 weeks of therapy:** epidural corticosteroid injection
**Disabling symptoms after 3–6 months or progressive motor deficit:** decompressive laminectomy
**MRI contraindicated:** CT myelography

UWSA1:Q034.boardCall: Twisting knee injury + delayed swelling + catching -> Painful click during knee extension and external rotation
UWSA1:Q034.hinge: Twisting trauma followed by delayed next-day swelling, joint-line pain with squatting, and mechanical catching indicates a meniscal tear.
UWSA1:Q034.trap: Immediate sharp pain tempts ACL rupture, but ACL tears produce rapid hemarthrosis within hours and instability rather than delayed swelling with mechanical catching.

A.fit: Not here: delayed next-morning swelling, catching sensation, twisting on foot

B.fit: Not here: catching and popping sensation on stairs and squatting

C.fit: Here: twisting injury, delayed swelling, medial pain with squatting and catching

D.clue: Synovial fluid collection in popliteal fossa
D.fit: Not here: acute traumatic onset with catching and medial pain
D.tempting: swelling behind knee from joint effusion

E.clue: Friction of iliotibial band over lateral epicondyle
E.fit: Not here: medial joint symptoms with catching, not lateral pain

F.fit: Not here: intraarticular catching sensation and mechanical clicking

nodes.text: Twisting injury, next-day swelling, joint-line pain, catching: meniscal tear
McMurray test (painful click with rotation) and Thessaly test
**Pop with hemarthrosis within hours, positive Lachman:** ACL tear instead
Radiographs to exclude fracture; MRI confirms tear
**Degenerative tear without locking:** exercise-based physical therapy + NSAIDs
**Locked knee or displaced tear:** arthroscopic repair or partial meniscectomy

UWSA1:Q035.boardCall: Painless bright red third-trimester bleeding + stable exam -> Transabdominal ultrasound
UWSA1:Q035.hinge: Sudden painless bright red vaginal bleeding in the third trimester requires immediate transabdominal ultrasound to localize the placenta; digital exam is contraindicated.
UWSA1:Q035.trap: Methamphetamine use strongly tempts placental abruption, but abruption causes painful bleeding with uterine tenderness and tetanic contractions, unlike the painless bleeding here.

A.clue: Manual digital palpation of cervical os and effacement
A.fit: Not here: strictly contraindicated in third-trimester bleeding until previa excluded

B.clue: Emergent operative delivery for fetal compromise
B.fit: Not here: hemodynamically stable mother with reassuring fetal tracing

C.clue: Biomarker assay predicting imminent preterm delivery
C.fit: Not here: gross vaginal bleeding invalidates fetal fibronectin assay

D.clue: Acid-elution test measuring fetomaternal hemorrhage volume
D.fit: Not here: first determine placental location before evaluating fetal red cell leak

E.clue: Antifibrinolytic agent stabilizing clot formation
E.fit: Not here: first-line evaluation is ultrasound localization of placenta

F.clue: Initial noninvasive sonography to localize placental position
F.fit: Here: 32 weeks, sudden painless bright red vaginal bleeding, reassuring FHR

nodes.text: Recognize third-trimester painless bright red bleeding: suspect placenta previa
Never perform digital cervical examination until placenta previa is ruled out
Immediate transabdominal ultrasound to determine placental location relative to internal os
**Unclear localization on transabdominal:** follow with transvaginal ultrasound
Continuous maternal vital signs and external fetal heart rate monitoring
**Active massive hemorrhage or nonreassuring fetal status:** emergent cesarean delivery
**Stable bleeding resolves at < 36 weeks:** expectant management + antenatal corticosteroids
Schedule elective cesarean delivery at 36 0/7 to 37 6/7 weeks for persistent previa

UWSA1:Q036.boardCall: Mediastinal mass + palmar hyperpigmentation + hypokalemic alkalosis -> Polypeptide hormone
UWSA1:Q036.hinge: Ectopic Cushing syndrome from a thoracic neuroendocrine tumor produces excessive ACTH, which is a 39-amino-acid polypeptide hormone.
UWSA1:Q036.trap: Clinical features of hypercortisolemia tempt steroid hormone (cortisol), but the mediastinal mass produces ACTH (a polypeptide), which secondarily stimulates cortisol.

A.clue: Catecholamines synthesized from tyrosine
A.fit: Not here: ACTH is a 39-amino-acid peptide cleaved from POMC

B.clue: Eicosanoids such as prostaglandins and leukotrienes
B.fit: Not here: ectopic ACTH is a polypeptide, not a lipid metabolite

C.clue: Peptide derived from proopiomelanocortin cleavage
C.fit: Here: mediastinal mass, palmar hyperpigmentation, BP 180/120, K 3.0 mEq/L

D.clue: Lipophilic hormone synthesized from cholesterol in adrenal cortex
D.fit: Not here: mass produces ACTH peptide, which then stimulates adrenal steroids
D.tempting: Cushing syndrome is characterized by high cortisol

E.clue: Secosteroid hormone such as 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D
E.fit: Not here: mediastinal tumor secretes ACTH polypeptide, not sterols

nodes.text: Rapid Cushing, hyperpigmentation, hypertension, hypokalemic alkalosis: suspect ectopic ACTH
Thoracic neuroendocrine tumor secretes ACTH, a POMC-derived polypeptide hormone
High ACTH + high urine free cortisol; no high-dose dexamethasone suppression
**Localized resectable tumor:** surgical resection
**Unresectable or occult tumor:** metyrapone, osilodrostat, or ketoconazole
**Cortisol uncontrolled despite steroidogenesis inhibitors:** bilateral adrenalectomy
Potassium repletion + spironolactone

UWSA1:Q037.boardCall: Post-thoracentesis shock + tachycardia + left chest dullness -> Decreased left ventricular preload
UWSA1:Q037.hinge: Acute hemorrhagic shock following thoracentesis severely reduces circulating blood volume and left ventricular preload.
UWSA1:Q037.trap: Removing 2 L of fluid tempts reexpansion pulmonary edema, but that causes diffuse crackles and hypoxia rather than massive unilateral dullness and profound hemorrhagic shock.

A.clue: Reduced ventricular end-diastolic volume from acute hypovolemia
A.fit: Here: post-thoracentesis BP 70 mm Hg, HR 130/min, left chest dullness

B.clue: Arterial vasodilation characteristic of distributive shock
B.fit: Not here: acute post-procedural hemorrhage produces high SVR and vasoconstriction

C.clue: Increased left ventricular filling pressure from cardiogenic failure
C.fit: Not here: acute hemorrhage depletes filling pressures, clear right hemithorax

D.clue: Mechanical obstruction to aortic outflow
D.fit: Not here: acute hypovolemic collapse following intercostal vascular injury

E.clue: Mechanical vascular occlusion from large pulmonary embolus
E.fit: Not here: unilateral chest dullness indicates massive fluid reaccumulation

nodes.text: Post-thoracentesis hypotension, tachycardia, new unilateral dullness: hemothorax
Intercostal artery laceration causes hemorrhage, decreasing LV preload
Crystalloid + PRBC transfusion; confirm with chest x-ray or ultrasound
Tube thoracostomy to evacuate blood and measure output
**Initial drainage > 1,500 mL or > 200 mL/h for 2–4 h:** thoracotomy
**Hyperresonance, absent breath sounds, tracheal deviation:** tension pneumothorax; needle decompression
**Elevated INR or anticoagulant use:** reverse coagulopathy
Serial hemoglobin and repeat chest imaging

UWSA1:Q038.boardCall: High-speed MVC + seat belt sign + widened mediastinum -> CT angiography of the chest
UWSA1:Q038.hinge: A widened mediastinum following high-speed deceleration blunt trauma indicates suspected blunt thoracic aortic injury, requiring immediate CT angiography in a stable patient.
UWSA1:Q038.trap: Normal lung exam and chest wall tenderness tempt musculoskeletal contusion managed with analgesics, but a widened mediastinum is aortic trauma until proven otherwise.

A.clue: Conservative supportive care for musculoskeletal chest contusion
A.fit: Not here: widened mediastinum indicates life-threatening aortic tear
A.tempting: normal breath sounds and soft abdomen

B.clue: Invasive catheter fluoroscopic imaging of thoracic aorta
B.fit: Not here: noninvasive CTA is faster and has replaced diagnostic aortography
B.tempting: historical gold standard for aortic injury

C.clue: Contrast-enhanced tomography to detect aortic pseudoaneurysm
C.fit: Here: high-speed deceleration, seat belt sign, widened mediastinum on CXR

D.clue: Emergent surgical open chest exploration
D.fit: Not here: patient is hemodynamically stable with BP 140/84 mm Hg

E.clue: Bedside ultrasound evaluating pericardial and valve anatomy
E.fit: Not here: poor sensitivity for thoracic aortic arch and descending isthmus

nodes.text: Recognize high-risk deceleration trauma: high-speed collision, seat belt sign, chest pain, tachycardia
Chest x-ray: assess for widened mediastinum (> 8 cm), abnormal aortic contour, or apical cap
**Hemodynamically stable with abnormal CXR or high mechanism:** CT angiography of the chest
**Hemodynamically unstable patient unable to travel to CT:** transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)
Initiate permissive hypotension: IV beta-blocker (esmolol) targeting SBP 100-120 and HR < 100
Definitive vascular management: thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) or open surgical repair

UWSA1:Q039.hinge: A painful, tender, fluctuant mass at the posterior vulva/base of the labium majus is a Bartholin gland abscess, treated with incision and drainage with Word catheter placement.
UWSA1:Q039.trap: Multiple sexual partners without barrier contraception tempts ceftriaxone plus doxycycline for an STI, but an isolated fluctuant abscess requires surgical drainage.

A.fit: Not here: fluctuant 3-cm labial mass, no painful vesicular ulcers
A.tempting: painful genital lesion in sexually active female

B.clue: Tissue sampling to exclude vulvar carcinoma
B.fit: Not here: 25-year-old with acute tender fluctuant abscess, not malignancy

C.clue: Antimicrobial coverage for gonorrhea and chlamydia cervicitis
C.fit: Not here: localized fluctuant Bartholin abscess, cervical os is normal
C.tempting: multiple sexual partners without barrier protection

D.clue: Surgical opening and evacuation of purulent collection
D.fit: Here: tender fluctuant 3-cm mass at base of right labium majus

E.clue: Radical surgical excision of mass with wide margins
E.fit: Not here: benign acute abscess, excision reserved for recurrent refractory cysts

nodes.text: A tender, fluctuant posterior vulvar mass indicates Bartholin gland abscess.
Perform incision and drainage with Word catheter placement.
Avoid incision alone or aspiration because early closure promotes recurrence.
**Cellulitis or systemic symptoms:** add antibiotics such as TMP-SMX or amoxicillin-clavulanate based on pathogen and patient factors.
**Recurrent abscess after catheter drainage:** perform marsupialization.
**Age ≥40 or suspicious mass:** obtain biopsy even if the lesion appears cystic.

UWSA1:Q040.boardCall: Adult frontal astrocytoma -> Degree of anaplasia
UWSA1:Q040.hinge: In astrocytomas, the degree of histologic anaplasia (cellular atypia, mitoses, necrosis) is the primary determinant of tumor grade and patient prognosis.
UWSA1:Q040.trap: In most systemic malignancies metastatic disease or tumor size dictates prognosis, but primary brain gliomas rarely metastasize extracranially and are graded by anaplasia.

A.clue: Maximum dimensional diameter of primary intracranial neoplasm
A.fit: Not here: histologic grade and anaplasia outweigh gross tumor size

B.clue: Dissemination of tumor cells outside central nervous system
B.fit: Not here: astrocytomas rarely metastasize outside the neural axis
B.tempting: primary prognostic factor in systemic cancers

C.clue: Histologic differentiation and cellular mitotic atypia
C.fit: Here: adult with newly diagnosed frontal lobe astrocytoma biopsy

D.clue: Specific cerebral lobe or functional anatomic region involved
D.fit: Not here: cellular anaplasia dictates aggressive biological behavior
D.tempting: frontal lobe location relates to operability

E.clue: Angioinvasion and tumor infiltration of cerebral blood vessels
E.fit: Not here: overall histologic anaplasia grade is the established predictor

nodes.text: New seizure, headache, focal deficit + enhancing mass: astrocytoma
Degree of anaplasia (atypia, mitoses, necrosis) sets grade and prognosis
Contrast MRI: extent, edema, mass effect
Maximal safe resection + molecular testing (IDH, MGMT)
**Grade 3–4 (including glioblastoma):** radiotherapy + temozolomide
**Grade 2 IDH-mutant with residual tumor:** vorasidenib or surveillance
**MGMT promoter methylated:** better temozolomide response and survival
Levetiracetam for seizures; dexamethasone for symptomatic edema

UWSA1:Q041.hinge: Transient stress-induced paranoia resolving within hours, combined with splitting and severe abandonment fears, defines borderline personality disorder.
UWSA1:Q041.trap: Belief that food was poisoned tempts primary psychotic disorder, but rapid resolution within hours following emotional conflict confirms borderline micropsychosis.

E.fit: Not here: no tachycardia, tremor, weight loss, or goiter on exam

nodes.text: Recognize borderline personality: abandonment fears, unstable relationships, splitting, stress paranoia
Distinguish transient stress-induced micropsychosis from primary schizophrenia spectrum disorders
First-line primary treatment: dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) or psychodynamic psychotherapy
**Acute severe agitation or transient psychotic symptoms:** short-term low-dose atypical antipsychotic
**Co-occurring major depressive or anxiety disorder:** add selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI)
Avoid benzodiazepines: high risk of behavioral disinhibition and lethal overdose
Establish clear therapeutic boundaries and maintain regular outpatient follow-up

nodes.text: Recognize Crohn disease: chronic abdominal pain, nonbloody diarrhea, weight loss, enterovaginal fistula
Ileocolonoscopy: cobblestone mucosa, skip lesions, aphthous ulcers, transmural inflammation
Pelvic MRI or CT enterography: identify fistula tracts and rule out pelvic abscess

D.clue: Continuous IV regular insulin with potassium repletion
D.fit: Here: post-bolus glucose 360, potassium 4.4 mEq/L, persistent ketonuria, pH 7.2

E.clue: Basal subcutaneous insulin during acute DKA
E.fit: Not here: acute DKA requires continuous IV regular insulin infusion rather than subcutaneous depot

F.clue: Subcutaneous short-acting insulin with oral potassium
F.fit: Not here: variable absorption in dehydrated patient necessitates continuous intravenous infusion

nodes.text: Initiate volume resuscitation with isotonic saline bolus over 1 hour
Start continuous intravenous regular insulin infusion with potassium-supplemented intravenous fluids
**Serum potassium < 3.3 mEq/L:** hold insulin and administer IV potassium until K > 3.3 mEq/L
**Serum glucose ≤ 200 mg/dL:** add 5% dextrose to intravenous fluids to prevent hypoglycemia and cerebral edema
**Severe acidemia with pH < 6.9:** consider slow infusion of isotonic sodium bicarbonate
Transition to subcutaneous insulin when anion gap closes (< 12 mEq/L), bicarbonate ≥ 15 mEq/L, and patient tolerates oral intake

triggers.text: receives 10 mL/kg of normal saline over 1 hour
Point-of-care urinalysis continues to show large ketones
Potassium 4.4 mEq/L
Glucose 360 mg/dL
Bicarbonate 12 mEq/L

UWSA1:Q088.boardCall: Chemotherapy nadir + fever ≥ 38.3 C + severe neutropenia (leukocytes 600/mm3) -> Systemic bacterial infection (neutropenic fever).
UWSA1:Q088.hinge: Febrile neutropenia 10 days post-chemotherapy is caused by systemic bacterial translocation across disrupted mucosal barriers.
UWSA1:Q088.trap: Chemotherapy, stents, or transfusion could suggest drug reaction or delayed hemolysis, but acute fever and profound neutropenia define neutropenic fever.

A.clue: Hypersensitivity drug reaction with fever and rash
A.fit: Not here: lack of rash, wheezing, or eosinophilia, with severe life-threatening neutropenia

B.clue: Anamnestic antibody-mediated extravascular hemolysis
B.fit: Not here: lack of jaundice, elevated indirect bilirubin, or direct antiglobulin positivity

C.clue: Cytokine release from bulky neoplastic tissue
C.fit: Not here: acute high fever and septic shock presentation during post-chemotherapy nadir

D.clue: Hyperuricemia, hyperkalemia, and hyperphosphatemia from cell lysis
D.fit: Not here: fever and neutropenia 10 days post-chemotherapy rather than immediate metabolic collapse

E.clue: Bacterial invasion during post-chemotherapy neutrophil nadir
E.fit: Here: fever 38.9 C, pulse 120, chemotherapy 10 days ago, leukocytes 600/mm3

nodes.text: Recognize febrile neutropenia: single oral temperature ≥ 38.3 C (101 F) with absolute neutrophil count < 500/mm3
Obtain immediate blood cultures from peripheral sites and indwelling central catheters
Promptly administer empiric broad-spectrum antipseudomonal monotherapy: cefepime, meropenem, or piperacillin-tazobactam
**Hemodynamic instability, catheter infection, or MRSA colonization:** add intravenous vancomycin
**Persistent fever after 4-7 days of antibacterial therapy:** add empiric antifungal therapy (voriconazole, caspofungin, or amphotericin B)
Continue antimicrobial therapy until neutrophil recovery (ANC > 500/mm3) and resolution of infection

triggers.text: completed the first cycle of combination chemotherapy 10 days ago
Temperature is 38.9 C (102 F)
Leukocytes 600/mm3
decreased oral intake and confusion
pulse is 120/min

UWSA1:Q089.boardCall: Woman > 40 + BMI 31 + epigastric/RUQ pain + fever + leukocytosis + normal lipase -> Acute cholecystitis.
UWSA1:Q089.hinge: Fever, leukocytosis, and acute constant epigastric pain with normal lipase and mildly elevated ALT indicate cystic duct obstruction.
UWSA1:Q089.trap: Epigastric pain radiating to back suggests pancreatitis, but serum lipase is completely normal.

A.clue: Cystic duct stone impaction with inflammation
A.fit: Here: 42yo woman, epigastric pain, fever 38.2 C, WBC 14,000, normal lipase

B.clue: Hepatocellular necroinflammation with transaminases in thousands
B.fit: Not here: transaminases AST 37 and ALT 79 are only minimally elevated
B.tempting: fever and mildly elevated liver enzymes

C.clue: Pancreatic acinar autodigestion with elevated lipase
C.fit: Not here: completely normal serum lipase level rules out acute pancreatitis
C.tempting: severe epigastric pain radiating to back

D.clue: Extrahepatic biliary obstruction with high direct bilirubin
D.fit: Not here: normal total bilirubin 1.0 mg/dL and alkaline phosphatase 90 U/L

E.clue: Chronic gastritis or peptic ulcer disease
E.fit: Not here: acute fever 38.2 C and leukocytosis 14,000/mm3 with systemic toxicity

F.clue: Statin-induced hepatic or muscular toxicity
F.fit: Not here: acute fever and leukocytosis with localized peritoneal signs

G.clue: Malignant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
G.fit: Not here: acute 3-hour onset with fever and leukocytosis in a 42-year-old
G.tempting: epigastric pain radiating to the back

nodes.text: Initial imaging: perform right upper quadrant abdominal ultrasound to assess gallbladder wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, and stones
**Equivocal ultrasound findings:** perform cholescintigraphy (HIDA scan) showing gallbladder nonvisualization
Maintain bowel rest (NPO) + intravenous fluids + IV broad-spectrum antibiotics (ceftriaxone + metronidazole)
Perform early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 72 hours of symptom onset
**Critically ill or high surgical risk patients:** place percutaneous cholecystostomy tube for gallbladder drainage
Monitor for complications: gallbladder gangrene, perforation, emphysematous cholecystitis, or gallstone ileus

triggers.text: severe epigastric pain for the past 3 hours
pain is constant and deep and radiates to the back
Temperature is 38.2 C (100.8 F)
Leukocytes 14,000/mm3
Serum lipase normal
radiates to the back

UWSA1:Q090.boardCall: Tension pneumothorax decompression -> decreases intrathoracic pressure -> increases systemic venous return (preload).
UWSA1:Q090.hinge: Decompressing trapped intrathoracic air relieves vena caval compression, restoring cardiac venous return and cardiac output.
UWSA1:Q090.trap: Restoring blood pressure may suggest increased contractility or vascular resistance, but the primary hemodynamic benefit is restoring venous return.

A.clue: Alveolar pressure remaining at end expiration
A.fit: Not here: needle decompression vents pleural air and does not increase PEEP

B.clue: Total circulating blood and fluid volume
B.fit: Not here: thoracostomy decompresses trapped air and does not administer fluid volume

C.clue: Inherent myocardial inotropic force
C.fit: Not here: intervention relieves external mechanical vascular compression without altering inotropy

D.clue: Resistance to forward blood flow from arterioles
D.fit: Not here: relieving obstructive shock increases cardiac output rather than systemic resistance

E.clue: Blood flow returning to the right atrium
E.fit: Here: tension pneumothorax with hypotension, tracheal deviation, absent sounds relieved by decompression

nodes.text: Distress, hypotension, unilateral absent breath sounds, tracheal deviation: tension pneumothorax
Rising intrathoracic pressure compresses vena cavae, cutting venous return and cardiac output
Immediate needle thoracostomy restores venous return
**Shock persists after needle decompression:** finger thoracostomy
**Normotensive without tracheal deviation:** upright CXR before chest tube
Tube thoracostomy for definitive evacuation
High-flow oxygen; CXR to confirm re-expansion

triggers.text: Blood pressure is 90/50 mm Hg and pulse is 118/min
Pulse oximetry is 88% on room air
neck veins are distended and the trachea is deviated to the right
Breath sounds are absent on the left side
involved in a motor vehicle collision

abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.name: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.scope: screening recommendations (men 65-75 who smoked), ultrasound imaging, surveillance intervals, elective repair thresholds, rupture
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.core: Older adult with abdominal aortic dilation may remain asymptomatic until expansion or rupture; sudden abdominal/back pain and hypotension require immediate vascular rescue.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking strongest modifiable risk; older age, male sex, family history, hypertension, atherosclerosis
Women have higher rupture risk at smaller diameters; most aneurysms infrarenal
Existing AAA: **diameter and high BP** predict rupture; cholesterol, A1c do not

rows.label: Clues
items: Incidental pulsatile expansile abdominal mass; localized persistent pain suggests symptomatic aneurysm
Rupture triad incompletely present; transient stability may reflect contained retroperitoneal hemorrhage
Blue toe/distal ischemia may result from mural thrombus embolization
Acute back pain unchanged by movement = **referred pain**; prevertebral calcification on x-ray; not disc disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Medial elastin/collagen degradation → progressive enlargement; greater wall radius increases tension

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Abdominal ultrasound** diagnoses AAA, generally diameter ≥3 cm; no contrast required
★ Stable suspected rupture or preoperative planning → **CT angiography**
Unstable suspected rupture → bedside ultrasound if immediate; no CT transport delaying surgery
Ultrasound detects aneurysm but cannot reliably exclude rupture; follow symptoms/hemodynamics

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Rupture → **urgent vascular repair**, IV access, blood products; avoid delaying for complete workup
Permissive hypotension during transfer/resuscitation until hemorrhage control when clinically feasible
★ Elective repair: **≥5.5 cm men, ≥5.0 cm women**, symptoms; **not if short life expectancy** (metastatic cancer)
Rapid growth ≥0.5 cm/6 months → repair consideration; endovascular versus open based on anatomy/fitness
Smaller asymptomatic lesions → ultrasound surveillance below; refer vascular surgery, manage cardiovascular risks

rows.label: Complications
items: Rupture, thrombosis, distal embolization; repair → AKI, bowel ischemia, endoleak after EVAR
Aortoenteric fistula after prior graft: herald GI bleed → catastrophic hemorrhage; urgent evaluation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **one-time ultrasound men 65–75 who ever smoked**; selectively screen never-smoking men
Women never smoked/no family history → no screening; women smokers/family history → USPSTF evidence insufficient
Smoking cessation, BP control, statin for atherosclerotic disease; lifelong imaging follow-up after EVAR

rows.label: Mimics
items: Renal colic: flank-to-groin pain, hematuria; shock atypical
Aortic dissection: abrupt chest/back pain, possible pulse deficits or branch ischemia

acid-base-disorders.name: Acid-base disorders
acid-base-disorders.scope: Metabolic acidosis (anion gap, non-anion gap), metabolic alkalosis (saline-responsive vs saline-resistant), respiratory acidosis, respiratory alkalosis, Winter formula, mixed disorders
acid-base-disorders.core: Identify the primary pH disturbance, test expected compensation, then investigate the anion gap or urine chloride to locate the cause.

rows.label: Definition
items: Acidemia: pH <7.35; alkalemia: >7.45; normal pH can hide opposing primary disorders
Metabolic: primary HCO3 change; respiratory: primary PaCO2 change

rows.label: Formula
items: ★ **AG = Na − (Cl + HCO3)**; usual normal ≈8–12, laboratory dependent
Hypoalbuminemia correction: add 2.5 to AG per 1 g/dL albumin below 4
★ **Winter: expected PaCO2 = 1.5 × HCO3 + 8 ±2**

rows.label: Interpret
items: HCO3 12 → expected PaCO2 26 ±2; measured 40 → additional respiratory acidosis
Metabolic alkalosis: expected PaCO2 ≈40 + 0.7 × (HCO3 − 24), ±5
Respiratory HCO3 change per 10 PaCO2: acidosis +1 acute/+4 chronic; alkalosis −2 acute/−4 chronic

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Alkalosis: **urine Cl <20 mmol/L** → saline-responsive; ≥20 → diuretics/mineralocorticoids
ΔAG exceeds HCO3 fall → additional alkalosis; smaller ΔAG → additional non-gap acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Compensation never overshoots; values outside expected range imply **mixed disorder**
Salicylates often cause respiratory alkalosis plus high-gap acidosis; near-normal pH is deceptive
Diarrhea/RTA: non-gap acidosis; distal RTA: urine pH >5.5, hypokalemia; renal failure: either gap pattern

acid-base-disorders.evidence: Established physiologic formulas; no guideline involved.

acute-agitation.name: Acute agitation
acute-agitation.scope: Verbal de-escalation, physical restraints, chemical restraints, intramuscular antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, QTc prolongation, medical workup
acute-agitation.core: Agitation is a symptom: protect immediate safety, use the least restrictive calming approach and search for a reversible medical cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Intoxication/withdrawal, psychosis, mania, delirium, dementia, hypoxia, hypoglycemia, pain
Recent medication change, infection, head trauma or inability to communicate needs

rows.label: Clues
items: Fluctuating attention/disorientation → delirium; hallucinations with intact attention can reflect primary psychosis
Diaphoresis, mydriasis, hypertension → stimulant intoxication; tremor/autonomic activation → withdrawal
Hyperthermia, rigidity, clonus, severe headache or focal deficit → toxic/neurologic emergency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Altered arousal and threat processing amplify behavior; sympathetic activation can worsen physiologic instability
Sedatives reduce motor activity but can conceal deterioration and impair ventilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Immediate **vital signs, pulse oximetry and fingerstick glucose**; assess trauma and toxidromes
Collateral history, medication list, focused neurologic/physical examination; assess attention and orientation
Target CBC, electrolytes, renal function, pregnancy/toxicology tests to findings; ECG before QT-prolonging drugs if feasible
Head CT for trauma, focal findings or unexplained altered mental status; never delay urgent stabilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Verbal de-escalation**: quiet space, one speaker, personal space, simple choices; offer oral drugs
★ Psychosis/mania, dangerous hyperactive delirium → **olanzapine or haloperidol**; IM if immediate danger, oral impossible
Stimulants, alcohol/benzodiazepine withdrawal or **QTc >500 ms** → **lorazepam**, no antipsychotic; monitor respiration
Avoid benzodiazepines in most delirium/depressant intoxication; **no IM olanzapine with parenteral benzodiazepines**
★ Imminent harm → brief physical restraints, continuous monitoring, frequent reassessment; remove promptly

rows.label: Complications
items: Hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, aspiration, sudden deterioration; positional restraint can cause asphyxia
Antipsychotics → QT prolongation, dystonia/NMS; benzodiazepines → respiratory depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Address pain, hunger, sensory impairment; reduce stimulation and preserve sleep
Use trauma-informed communication, staff training and individualized crisis plans

rows.label: Mimics
items: Akathisia: medication-linked inner restlessness; escalating antipsychotics worsens symptoms
Catatonia: posturing, negativism or stereotypy; lorazepam-responsive syndrome

acute-agitation.evidence: Not checked online; established emergency psychiatry and restraint principles.

acute-coronary-syndromes.name: Acute coronary syndromes
acute-coronary-syndromes.scope: Unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI, cardiac biomarkers, risk stratification (HEART/TIMI), antiplatelet and anticoagulation, reperfusion
acute-coronary-syndromes.core: Acute myocardial ischemia from coronary plaque disruption: distinguish occlusive infarction needing immediate reperfusion from non-ST-elevation syndromes needing risk-guided invasive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, age, premature family CAD
Cocaine/stimulants, anemia, tachyarrhythmia may provoke ischemia; distinguish supply-demand injury from plaque rupture

rows.label: Clues
items: Pressure with arm/jaw radiation, diaphoresis, nausea; older adults/diabetes may have dyspnea or epigastric pain alone
Inferior MI with hypotension, clear lungs, raised JVP → suspect RV infarction
★ New murmur, pulmonary edema, shock after MI → **mechanical complication**, urgent echo
Unexplained crash/syncope + ischemic ECG → primary MI; troponin over trauma imaging

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet activation and thrombin-mediated clot reduce coronary perfusion; necrosis releases troponin
Type 2 MI: oxygen mismatch without acute atherothrombosis; treat precipitating cause

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG within 10 minutes**, repeat if nondiagnostic; serial high-sensitivity troponin using validated pathway
Posterior suspicion → V7–V9; inferior MI → right-sided leads; new LBBB alone insufficient for STEMI
★ **Do not wait for troponin before STEMI reperfusion**; bedside echo if diagnosis/complications uncertain
HEART ≤3 + negative serial troponins → low risk; TIMI/GRACE stratifies NSTE-ACS
STE: **V1–V6 → LAD**; **II, III, aVF + bradycardia → RCA**; I, aVL → circumflex

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Chewed aspirin**, P2Y12 inhibitor, anticoagulant such as heparin, high-intensity atorvastatin; oxygen only if hypoxemic
Nitroglycerin (**venodilation** → ↓preload) for pain unless hypotension, RV infarction, recent PDE5 inhibitor; avoid NSAIDs
★ STEMI → **primary PCI** within 90 minutes at PCI center, ≤120 minutes including transfer
IF PCI delay >120 minutes, symptoms <12 hours, no contraindication → fibrinolysis promptly, then transfer

rows.label: Complications
items: VT/VF, AV block, HF, cardiogenic shock; free-wall rupture
Later aneurysm/thrombus, embolism, Dressler syndrome; antithrombotics → bleeding
Post-MI murmur: **papillary rupture** → apical, no O₂ step-up; **septal rupture** → left sternal, RA→RV step-up

rows.label: Prevention
items: DAPT usually 12 months after ACS unless bleeding risk changes plan; cardiac rehabilitation, smoking cessation
ACE inhibitor/ARB for LV dysfunction; beta-blocker when stable, avoid in shock or acute decompensation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aortic dissection: abrupt tearing pain/pulse deficit; anticoagulation or lysis dangerous
Pericarditis: positional pleuritic pain, diffuse changes
PE: hypoxemia, thrombotic risk, RV strain

table.title: Syndrome branches
rows: Urgent catheterization if unstable; otherwise risk-guided angiography
Regional ST elevation or occlusion equivalent
Prior intracranial hemorrhage, active bleeding, suspected dissection
Stress or perfusion testing within 72 hours

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all 19–59; ≥60 with risk/request; health worker anti-HBs negative post-series → revaccinate
**HIV any CD4**, liver disease/alcohol, COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal <50; liver → HepA/HepB
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Anti-HBs/anti-HAV/VZV IgG positive → immune, skip; otherwise **do not delay vaccination** for serology
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza**: severe immunosuppression, pregnancy (nonimmune → postpartum)
PCV15 → PPSV23: ≥8 weeks immunocompromised; older exams: PPSV23 alone; mild illness/antibiotics: no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern; inactivated influenza cannot cause flu, coincidental virus; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

alcohol-withdrawal.name: Alcohol withdrawal
alcohol-withdrawal.core: Autonomic and neuropsychiatric excitation after reducing prolonged heavy alcohol intake; progression from mild symptoms to life-threatening delirium.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior withdrawal seizures/delirium, repeated detoxifications, heavy sustained use, older age
Acute illness, electrolyte depletion, concurrent sedative dependence; poor support increases outpatient failure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Diaphoresis, tachycardia, hypertension, insomnia, nausea; symptoms possible with **positive blood alcohol**
Hospital day 2–5 or postoperative: new agitation, hallucinations, autonomic signs → suspect **unreported alcohol use**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Chronic ethanol → downregulated GABA inhibition/upregulated NMDA excitation; cessation unmasks neuronal hyperactivity
Repeated episodes → kindling, progressively lower seizure threshold

rows.label: Dx
items: **Clinical diagnosis** + time since reduction; bedside glucose, CBC, electrolytes, Mg, phosphate, liver tests
★ **CIWA-Ar** if communicative; ≥19 severe; delirium/intubation → **RASS/MINDS**
First/focal seizure, head injury, focal deficit, atypical timing → head CT; do not assume withdrawal

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Diazepam/chlordiazepoxide** symptom-triggered; liver dysfunction/older frail adults → **lorazepam/oxazepam**
★ Seizures/delirium → monitored inpatient **IV benzodiazepines**; refractory → ICU phenobarbital with respiratory monitoring
★ **Parenteral thiamine**; hypoglycemia → immediate dextrose, never wait; correct electrolyte deficits
Phenytoin ineffective; dexmedetomidine adjunct; **chlorpromazine**/antipsychotics lower seizure threshold, prolong QT

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration, dysrhythmias, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis; excessive sedation → respiratory depression
Malnutrition → Wernicke encephalopathy: confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia; suspected → high-dose IV thiamine
Pregnancy: seizures, adrenergic surge → fetal hypoxia; **maternal withdrawal** is greatest immediate fetal risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: High-risk inpatients → preventive benzodiazepines; outpatient withdrawal only if mild, reliable supervision
Recovery: **naltrexone** unless opioids/acute hepatitis; **acamprosate** unless severe CKD; addiction follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hepatic encephalopathy: asterixis, decompensated cirrhosis, less autonomic excitation
Sepsis: infectious source, hypotension, persistent inflammatory findings
Sedative withdrawal: benzodiazepine/barbiturate reduction; similar syndrome, different exposure
Anticholinergic delirium: dry skin, urinary retention; diaphoresis favors withdrawal

table.title: Approximate onset after reduction; overlap common
rows: Visual/auditory/tactile hallucinations; clear sensorium; vitals near normal
Disorientation, hallucinations, fever, tremor, marked autonomic instability

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization
Galactorrhea, hypothyroid signs → TSH first (TRH raises prolactin); unexplained prolactin → pituitary MRI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow
Functional: energy deficit disrupts pulsatile GnRH → irregular, low gonadotropins, low estrogen

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even if unlikely or premenarchal (ovulation precedes menarche); ultrasound assesses uterus, ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; low estradiol: high FSH → ovarian failure; low/normal FSH → hypothalamic/pituitary
**Progestin challenge**: bleed → anovulation (estrogen, outflow intact); no bleed → low estrogen/outflow defect, check FSH
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause
Hematocolpos → **transvaginal incision, drainage**; imperforate hymen → **cruciate hymenotomy**; ultrasound if anatomy unclear

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

table.title: Primary amenorrhea: high FSH or absent uterus → karyotype

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.scope: Upper and lower motor neuron signs, bulbar symptoms, preserved sensation, EMG/NCS findings, noninvasive positive pressure ventilation, riluzole, edaravone, end-of-life planning
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.core: Progressive weakness with upper and lower motor neuron signs in multiple regions, usually with preserved sensation and sphincter function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Middle/older adulthood, male sex; mostly sporadic, minority familial
Family history of motor neuron disease or frontotemporal dementia supports inherited susceptibility

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Atrophy, fasciculations + hyperreflexia/spasticity** within affected regions; asymmetric limb onset common
Bulbar disease: dysarthria, dysphagia, tongue wasting; pseudobulbar affect may accompany corticobulbar dysfunction
Orthopnea, morning headache, weak cough → ventilatory weakness; inward abdominal motion on inspiration → **diaphragmatic paralysis**
Ocular movement and sensation usually spared; some patients develop executive or behavioral impairment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Degeneration of corticospinal neurons and anterior horn/bulbar motor neurons; denervation spreads progressively

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical progression + EMG/NCS**: widespread **fibrillation potentials**, sharp waves, chronic denervation; sensory conduction normal
MRI brain/spine to exclude structural mimics; targeted B12, thyroid, CK, and other studies
Assess FVC, inspiratory strength, nocturnal gas exchange, swallow function, nutrition; no single definitive blood test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Riluzole** modestly prolongs survival; edaravone may slow functional decline in selected patients
★ **Noninvasive ventilation** for symptomatic respiratory weakness improves comfort and survival
Swallow/nutrition support; discuss gastrostomy before severe respiratory decline; cough-assist and secretion management
Baclofen for spasticity, communication devices, physical/occupational support; multidisciplinary specialty care
Early shared planning for ventilation, feeding, advance directives, hospice; discuss choices before communication declines

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure is usual terminal event; aspiration, malnutrition, falls, immobility
Depression, caregiver burden; frontotemporal impairment may affect decision-making capacity

rows.label: Prevention
items: No primary prevention; aspiration/fall precautions, vaccination, nutritional support, respiratory surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical myelopathy: sensory level, sphincter changes, compressive MRI lesion
Myasthenia gravis: fatigable ocular weakness, no UMN signs
Multifocal motor neuropathy: conduction block, IVIG response

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.evidence: Not checked online; established ALS diagnosis and supportive-treatment teaching.

antepartum-bleeding.name: Antepartum bleeding
antepartum-bleeding.scope: Placenta previa, placental abruption, vasa previa, uterine rupture, transabdominal ultrasound before digital exam, Kleihauer-Betke test, emergent cesarean delivery
antepartum-bleeding.core: Bleeding in later pregnancy requires immediate maternal stabilization and fetal assessment, followed by placental localization before any digital cervical examination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previa: prior cesarean, multiparity; abruption: hypertension, cocaine, trauma, prior abruption
Vasa previa: velamentous cord, accessory placental lobe, IVF; rupture: uterine scar, obstructed labor

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Shock may exceed visible blood loss** with concealed abruption or internal hemorrhage
Assess uterine tone, pain, contractions, fetal tracing, membrane status; bleeding volume alone is unreliable

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maternal placental bleeding versus fetal vessel hemorrhage; vasa previa can rapidly exsanguinate fetus
Placental separation or uterine disruption compromises oxygen delivery independent of maternal external blood loss

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ CBC, type/crossmatch, coagulation studies including fibrinogen; continuous fetal monitoring if viable
★ **Ultrasound before digital examination**; transabdominal first; transvaginal safely clarifies placenta–cervix relationship
Normal ultrasound does not exclude abruption; suspected rupture is a clinical emergency
Rh-negative bleeding/trauma → Kleihauer–Betke or flow cytometry quantifies fetomaternal hemorrhage for anti-D dosing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ ABCs, two large IVs, blood products when needed; **do not delay delivery for imaging if unstable**
Hemorrhage/fetal compromise → emergency cesarean; rupture → laparotomy, uterine repair or hysterectomy
Stable preterm previa → observation, pelvic rest, corticosteroids when eligible; planned cesarean before labor
Abruption: deliver if significant or compromised; vaginal birth possible when stable and imminent or fetal demise
Unsensitized Rh-negative patient → anti-D immunoglobulin; correct abruption-associated coagulopathy

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhagic shock, DIC, AKI, hysterectomy; fetal hypoxia, death, prematurity
Previa plus cesarean scar increases placenta accreta spectrum risk and operative hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP, avoid cocaine/tobacco; prenatal placental/cord localization and planned high-risk delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bloody show: small mucus-streaked bleeding with cervical change
Cervical lesion: contact bleeding, visible source on speculum examination

table.title: Critical distinctions
rows: Bleeding after rupture; sudden fetal bradycardia
Scarred uterus; sudden pain, lost station, fetal bradycardia

antepartum-bleeding.evidence: Not checked online; established obstetric hemorrhage teaching.

antipsychotics.name: Antipsychotics
antipsychotics.scope: First-generation vs second-generation, extrapyramidal symptoms (acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia), neuroleptic malignant syndrome, metabolic syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, QTc prolongation
antipsychotics.core: Dopamine-modulating drugs treat psychosis and mania; selection depends on motor, metabolic, endocrine, cardiovascular, and hematologic risks.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ Psychosis, mania, agitation; **SGA first-line**; **clozapine** if resistant or recurrent suicidality
FGA: mainly D2 antagonism; SGA: D2/5-HT2 effects, varying by agent
Quetiapine sedation → switch to aripiprazole; obesity → ziprasidone, not olanzapine/clozapine

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Nigrostriatal blockade → movement disorders; tuberoinfundibular blockade → prolactin elevation
Aripiprazole: partial D2 agonist; haloperidol high-potency FGA, chlorpromazine low-potency FGA
Chronic D2 blockade → receptor supersensitivity → tardive dyskinesia; can worsen after stopping

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Fever, **lead-pipe rigidity**, autonomic instability, high CK → NMS; stop drug, supportive ICU care
Severe NMS: dantrolene/bromocriptine; olanzapine/clozapine: weight gain, diabetes, dyslipidemia
Risperidone: ↑prolactin; ziprasidone: ↑QT; clozapine: neutropenia, myocarditis, ileus, seizures

rows.label: Avoid
items: Lewy body/Parkinson disease: severe sensitivity; specialist-selected quetiapine/clozapine if essential
Dementia: ↑mortality, falls; dangerous behavior after safer measures → low-dose **quetiapine**/risperidone, not benzodiazepines

rows.label: Interactions
items: Other QT-prolonging drugs, electrolyte depletion → torsades; sedatives/alcohol increase CNS depression
Metoclopramide, prochlorperazine block dopamine: same EPS, tardive dyskinesia, NMS; avoid after NMS

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Weight/BMI, BP, glucose/A1c, lipids; movement examinations; **ANC with clozapine**
ECG for cardiac/QT risks; prolactin when symptomatic; ask about bowel function
Clozapine + ANC <1000 → **hold clozapine**, not dose reduction; ANC 1000–1499 → continue, closer monitoring

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Anticholinergics worsen tardive dyskinesia**; valbenazine/deutetrabenazine are VMAT2 inhibitors
Akathisia can mimic worsening agitation; increasing antipsychotic dose can worsen it
Low-potency FGAs: more orthostasis/anticholinergic effects; high-potency FGAs: more EPS

table.title: Extrapyramidal syndromes
rows: Stop/switch culprit first; benztropine or amantadine

antipsychotics.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [FDA clozapine monitoring update](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-removes-risk-evaluation-and-mitigation-strategy-rems-program-antipsychotic-drug-clozapine); other effects established teaching.

asplenia.name: Asplenia
asplenia.scope: Anatomic asplenia (splenectomy), functional asplenia (sickle cell), Howell-Jolly bodies, reactive thrombocytosis, encapsulated organism sepsis (Streptococcus pneumoniae), vaccination timing, antibiotic prophylaxis
asplenia.core: Absent or poorly functioning spleen impairs clearance of encapsulated organisms; fever can progress rapidly to fatal sepsis despite prior vaccination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Splenectomy for trauma/hematologic disease; functional loss with sickle cell disease; congenital absence
Sepsis risk greatest early after surgery and in children, but remains lifelong

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Fever, rigors, malaise, vomiting, or rapid deterioration → **overwhelming postsplenectomy infection**
Pneumococcus especially important; also meningococcus, Hib; dog bites risk Capnocytophaga
Travel-associated malaria and Babesia can become unusually severe

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Loss of splenic macrophage filtration and IgM memory B-cell function impairs opsonized-organism clearance
Reduced removal of erythrocyte inclusions and platelets explains characteristic blood findings

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Smear: **Howell–Jolly bodies**; reactive thrombocytosis after splenectomy; correlate with history/imaging
Febrile illness → cultures, CBC, lactate, source evaluation; do not delay antibiotics for results
Unexplained anemia/fever after tick exposure or travel → smear/PCR for intraerythrocytic parasites

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected sepsis → **immediate ceftriaxone**, add vancomycin for severe/resistant pneumococcal concern
Resuscitate and admit if ill; even initially mild fever requires urgent clinical evaluation
Standby oral antibiotic if immediate care inaccessible, followed by emergency evaluation; not a substitute for assessment
Daily penicillin/amoxicillin in young children, particularly sickle cell disease through at least age 5

rows.label: Complications
items: Fulminant bacteremia, meningitis, purpura fulminans, DIC, death
Postoperative thrombosis risk; isolated reactive platelet elevation does not automatically require antiplatelet treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Vaccinate **≥14 days before elective splenectomy**; after emergency surgery vaccinate once stable
Adult antibiotic prophylaxis individualized by postoperative period, immune status, and prior invasive infection
Medical alert ID, fever plan, influenza vaccination; bite counseling, travel precautions and malaria prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Iron deficiency: reactive thrombocytosis without splenic dysfunction
Hyposplenism: spleen present but impaired; similar infection precautions

table.title: Vaccine priorities: unvaccinated adults
rows: One dose if not previously vaccinated

atrial-fibrillation.name: Atrial fibrillation
atrial-fibrillation.scope: Rate and rhythm control, stroke prevention (CHA2DS2-VASc), unstable AF, embolic complications
atrial-fibrillation.core: Disorganized atrial activation produces an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm and left atrial appendage thromboembolism risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, hypertension, heart failure, coronary disease, obesity, sleep apnea
Hyperthyroidism, alcohol binges, infection, postoperative stress, mitral valve disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Palpitations, exercise intolerance, dyspnea; sometimes incidental or first detected after stroke
